findings.title: Reminder phone_map routes clinic WhatsApp to another therapist's patient by forged appointment name
findings.attacker: An authenticated therapist who can create tomorrow-dated appointments they own under Firestore rules.
findings.controlled_input: appointments/{id}.name matching a peer therapist's patient display name, with missing or invalid profileId/patientId.
findings.attack_path: Peer therapist has a tomorrow appointment with profileId set. Reminder cron preloads that profile into phone_map keyed by name.lower(). Attacker creates an owned tomorrow appointment with the same name (and garbage/missing profileId). execute_send_reminders / execute_send_evening_reminders resolve the attacker appointment via the shared name key and Twilio-send the real parent's WhatsApp a clinic reminder for the forged slot/therapist.
findings.impact: Cross-therapist unsolicited WhatsApp to a real parent with attacker-controlled schedule details under clinic branding; increases chance of mistaken confirm/cancel via existing name matching.
findings.evidence: Previously phone_map[data.name.lower()]=data when loading by profileId; lookup fell back to phone_map[p_name.lower()]. Repo now uses _load_reminder_profiles_by_id (id-only) and _resolve_reminder_profile with same-therapist name fallback.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not webhook confirm/cancel name matching; not Autopilot candidate name lookup. This is outbound reminder destination confusion via a shared name index built from other appointments' profileIds.
findings.remediation: Deploy functions. Prefer requiring profileId on reminder-eligible appointments; disallow therapist field reassignment without isOwner(new).

findings.title: Therapist-reassigned planted evaluation appointments hijack Diana eval WhatsApp and clinical stage flags
findings.attacker: An authenticated therapist who can update appointments they currently own.
findings.controlled_input: appointments/{id}.isEvaluation, .evaluationStage, .profileId, .date (earlier today), then .therapist set to diana in an owner-authorized update.
findings.attack_path: Create an evaluation appointment under the attacker therapist key. Update therapist to diana (rules authorize isOwner on pre-update therapist only). At 21:00 MX, execute_send_diana_evaluation_followup sends Diana the E2 WhatsApp template with attacker-controlled name/stage. If Diana responds eval_yes/eval_entrega (or the first matching awaiting profile is processed), handlers set dianaSession* and awaitingDianaNextStage/evaluationStage without verifying the bound profile is Diana's patient.
findings.impact: Clinic-branded WhatsApp spam/phishing to Diana's phone and corruption of evaluation workflow flags.
findings.evidence: execute_send_diana_evaluation_followup and _find_diana_eval_apt_today previously only checked appointments.therapist==diana. Repo adds _profile_therapist_is(profileId,'diana') gates and filters awaitingDianaNextStage to Diana-owned profiles.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Distinct from Autopilot cancel→peer therapist offers and from calendar sync unknown-therapist→Diana OAuth event writes. This path is Diana eval E2/E3 templates and patientProfiles evaluation flags.
findings.remediation: Deploy functions. Add Firestore rules isOwner(request.resource.data.therapist) and enum therapist keys.
